description: We are RARS The Explorers, a multidisciplinary team passionate about biomedical engineering, hardware-software integration, and aerospace health tech. We developed HELIX, an autonomous crew telemetry and biometric command suite for deep-space missions. We bring skills in full-stack development, IoT, and biomedical systems design to innovate in space exploration and human health technology!
summary:
HELIX (Autonomous Crew Telemetry & Biometric Command Suite) is an offline-capable, web-based health monitoring and decision-support system designed for deep-space missions like Artemis and Mars transit.
1. What we developed: A comprehensive, single-file space command application featuring real-time biometric tracking (heart rate, SpO₂, temperature, and radiation), a multimodal computer vision module for drowsiness detection and exercise/hydration verification, an AI flight surgeon assistant, and a NASA Ames Bayesian belief network for predictive hazard modeling.
2. How it addresses the challenge: Because deep-space communication suffers from severe light-time delays exceeding 20 minutes with Earth, HELIX operates entirely autonomously. It uses an offline-first architecture that processes telemetry locally, triggers immediate haptic wristband alerts, and bundles data for delayed deep-space network (DSN) downlinks.
3. Why it is important: It ensures astronaut safety and operational readiness millions of miles from Earth, mitigating critical spaceflight hazards such as cardiovascular strain, rapid fluid shifts, circadian sleep debt, and solar radiation events without requiring real-time ground control.
details:
1. What does it do & How does it work?

HELIX is an autonomous, offline-capable medical and telemetry command suite built for deep-space missions (such as Artemis and Mars transit). Because deep-space communication suffers from severe light-time delays (up to 20+ minutes one-way with Earth), HELIX operates independently of real-time ground control.

It continuously monitors astronaut vital signs (heart rate, blood oxygen, core temperature, and radiation dosage via simulated UWB wristbands), uses computer vision to track eye states (drowsiness/micro-sleep detection) and verify 0g physical exercise and fluid intake, and implements automated NASA standards rule-checking.

2. What benefits does it have?

- Eliminates reliance on real-time Earth communication for mission-critical health triage.

- Provides instant, automated local haptic feedback and warning alarms when physiological parameters breach safety limits.

- Enables secure, private biometric and PIN-gated individual astronaut medical decks.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

To safeguard astronaut health and operational readiness during long-duration spaceflight, minimizing the risk of cardiovascular strain, extreme fluid shifts, circadian sleep debt, and solar particle radiation events.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

- Frontend & Architecture: Single-file client-side web application built with, pycharm, claude,python HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, styled with a high-contrast dark-theme space command aesthetic.

- Simulation & AI Logic: Embedded heuristic client-side rule engines, camera-based web APIs for multimodal computer vision tracking, and automated NASA Ames Bayesian belief network (BBN) calculations for spaceflight hazard prediction (such as SANS and nephrolithiasis).

- Deployment: Hosted statically via modern cloud infrastructure

5. How is your project creative & What factors did your team consider?

- Creativity: It bridges aerospace engineering with user-friendly web design by transforming complex aerospace physiology standards (NASA-STD-3001) into an interactive, gamified, and fully functional sci-fi command suite.

- Key Factors Considered: Team design focused heavily on latency resilience (offline-first architecture), data privacy (dual-factor Face ID & PIN gate for private health decks), and rigorous adherence to real-world spaceflight human research program (HRP) guidelines.
